PromQL: store WITHOUT labels as strings, not Attributes

WITHOUT labels are filter keys for _timeseries output - they don't need
resolution to FieldAttribute. Store them as Set<String> in
AcrossSeriesAggregate.withoutLabels() instead of List<Attribute>.

This simplifies the design and fixes #149793 where UnresolvedAttributes
couldn't be resolved and were filtered out by dimensionAttributes().

Changes:
- AcrossSeriesAggregate: add withoutLabels field (Set<String>)
- UnresolvedPromqlFunction: add withoutLabels field
- Parser: pass strings for WITHOUT, attributes only for BY
- LabelSetSpec: use Set<String> for exclusions
- TimeSeriesWithout: add constructor for label names
- Remove Analyzer workaround for resolving groupings

Closes #149793

The WITHOUT clause labels are filter keys for _timeseries output.
Previously, LabelSetSpec.dimensionAttributes() and
TimeSeriesWithout.excludedFieldNames() only extracted names from
FieldAttribute instances, filtering out UnresolvedAttributes.

Fix by accepting any Attribute type:
- LabelSetSpec.dedupeByFieldName() extracts names from all Attributes
- TimeSeriesWithout.excludedFieldNames() falls back to Attribute.name()

Turbopack's analyzer: always treat promises as truth-y and non-nullish (#94186)

Promises are not included in the list of JavaScript's falsy values,
therefore, they are always truthy. See
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Truthy. Additionally,
promises are neither `null` or `undefined` so they are not nullish:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Nullish_coalescing.

This PR updates Turbopack's analyzer to reflect this + adds unit tests
for `is_truthy` and `is_nullish`.

therefore, they are always truthy. See
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Truthy. Additionally,
promises are neither `null` or `undefined` so they are not nullish:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Nullish_coalescing.

This PR updates Turbopack's analyzer to reflect this + adds unit tests
for `is_truthy` and `is_nullish`.

This shrinks the proc-macro ABI a bit. Nothing on the client side needs
to allocate handles. This will share the counters between proc-macros,
which may cause us to run out of handles earlier, but 4 bilion handles
per process is still a lot. Rust-analyzer might run out at some point,
but it can recover by restarting the proc-macro-server, and it could
already run out before this change anyway,

Make Linux desktop sanity tests robust to mid-test failures

The Linux desktop sanity tests (deb/rpm/snap) ran cleanup unconditionally
after `testDesktopApp` without a try/finally, so when that step threw
(e.g. extension install flake tracked in microsoft/vscode-engineering#2877)
the uninstall step was skipped. Mocha then retried the test, the install
step hit `package code-insiders is already installed`, and the retry
masked the real failure with a misleading error
(microsoft/vscode-engineering#2878).

Fix:
- Wrap install/test/uninstall in try/finally so cleanup runs even when
  the test body throws.
- Make the uninstall helpers idempotent by detecting whether the package
  binary exists; this lets the finally block run safely even if install
  itself fails (and avoids double-uninstall on the happy path).
- Add a pre-install assertion to each install helper that fails fast
  with a clear diagnostic when the package is already present, so any
  leftover state from a prior killed run su

fix: NPE on null zeroTermsQuery in cross_fields query (#149935) (#150137)

* Guard against null zeroTermsQuery in cross_fields

#143220 added query.visit(queryVisitor) after the
zeroTermsQuery.asQuery() fallback to enforce the boolean
clause limit during query construction. asQuery() returns
null for ZeroTermsQueryOption.NONE, so the unconditional
visit() call throws NullPointerException whenever a token
in a cross_fields query_string analyzes to zero terms (for
example a stopword on a stopword-stripping analyzer).

The sibling MatchQueryParser was updated with a null guard
in the same PR; mirror it here. Adds a regression test that
exercises both the NONE and ALL branches of the fallback.

policy: enforce enabledPlugins/strictMarketplaces for Copilot-CLI plugins

CLI-installed plugins under `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>/`
have no `fromMarketplace` metadata, so they previously bypassed enterprise
policy. Derive their identity from the install-path bucket (matching the
convention used by `_resolveEnterprisePluginId`) so enabledPlugins gating
applies, and add a bucket-name heuristic for strict marketplaces.

Hot-reload workload-identity client SSL

Previously, rotating the workload-identity issuer client's
certificate or key required a node restart.

Watch the files referenced by workload_identity.ssl.* via
ResourceWatcherService and rebuild the SSLContext on change.
A ReloadableSchemeIoSessionStrategy wrapper registered against
"https" on the HC connection manager lets reload swap the
SSLIOSessionStrategy in place rather than rebuilding the
CloseableHttpAsyncClient, so in-flight requests are not aborted.

Each handshake stamps the IOSession with a monotonic rotation
epoch; a RotationAwareReuseStrategy retires connections whose
stamp no longer matches the current epoch as their next response
completes, bounding drain to one request-response cycle per
connection regardless of load shape.

Add brackets opt-in to external-basic {{books}} queries

The repoint of external-basic.csv-spec to {{employees_no_mv}} (scalar
twin) covered the 67 employees-fixture references but missed 4 queries
that read {{books}} for RERANK / TOP_SNIPPETS / SCORE testing:
- externalRerankBooks
- topSnippetsFunction
- scoreFunction
- (one more in the same family)

The books fixture has its own bracket-MV column (authors:
[Fyodor Dostoevsky, Alan Myers, W. J. Leatherbarrow]). Under the new
multi_value_syntax: none default, the CSV reader splits at the commas
inside [...] -> 11 columns on the affected row vs 9 expected, then
fails the read because error_mode isn't set.

GenerativeForkIT was the first IT to surface this -- single-node
EsqlSpecIT runs with cap-filter that skipped these tests, but the
generative fork variant includes them and they fail at parse time.

Fix: add explicit WITH {"multi_value_syntax": "brackets"} opt-in to
all 4 {{books}} reads in external-basic.csv-spec, same pattern as the
PR feedback

[hack] ZJIT: Insert NoEpEscape after each safepoint `Effect::write(abstract_heaps::Frame)`

This is a hacky fix for https://github.com/Shopify/ruby/issues/970.
I initially tried to do it as a pass, but then thought I wouldn't have
access to the right snapshots to construct a
`Invariant::NoEPEscape($snapshot_id)`, so I moved the logic to
iseq_to_hir. It's actually possible to find yarv insn boundaries
post-hoc by scanning backwards for snapshots -- they're present until
DCE. It's better to insert these PPs post-hoc, after strength reduction,
because it may remove safepoint insns. We really want to insert PPs as
late as possible since once they're in nothing removes them.

Doing it in a pass may require dominance info to get right. Consider
yarv insns expanding to a diamond and loops.

access to the right snapshots to construct a
`Invariant::NoEPEscape($snapshot_id)`, so I moved the logic to
iseq_to_hir. It's actually possible to find yarv insn boundaries
post-hoc by scanning backwards for snapshots -- they're present until
DCE. It's better to insert these PPs post-hoc, after strength reduction,
because it may remove safepoint insns. We really want to insert PPs as
late as possible since once they're in nothing removes them.

Doing it in a pass may require dominance info to get right. Consider
yarv insns expanding to a diamond and loops.

preserve marketplace name through managed_settings policy delivery

The managed_settings adapter previously flattened extraKnownMarketplaces
entries to bare "<owner>/<repo>" or "<url>" strings, losing the marketplace
name. That broke enabledPlugins matching because plugin IDs are keyed as

- IPolicyData.extraKnownMarketplaces accepts string | object entries
- parseMarketplaceReferences gains object-handling, using name as displayLabel
- workspacePluginSettingsService shares the object parser
- policy schema relaxed to allow object items

Validate inference embedding model before checking for existing uses

This commit changes the order of two steps when creating an inference
endpoint in TransportPutInferenceModelAction. The validation call is now
performed prior to checking for existing index mappings using the
inference endpoint ID, since if dimensions are not specified by the user

create a MinimalServiceSettings from the request will throw, because
dimensions are required in the MinimalServiceSettings constructor.

call to updateModelWithEmbeddingDetails(), meaning that the dimensions
are guaranteed to be non-null when TransportPutInferenceModelAction
checks for existing uses of the inference endpoint ID.

policy: accept host-only git URLs in extraKnownMarketplaces

ADR-002 describes the `git` source `url` as a free-form `(string)`
the example happens to be a full clone URL, but the schema doesn't
require a repo path. Our marketplace-URI parser was rejecting host-only
HTTPS endpoints (e.g. `https://plugins.internal.example.com`), so
enterprise policy entries with marketplace-registry-style URLs were
silently dropped before they ever reached the UI.

Relax `parseUriMarketplaceReference` to accept host-only URLs and
treat them as a marketplace endpoint identified by host alone. The
canonical id becomes `git:<host>/` so distinct hosts still dedupe
correctly. Existing path-aware behavior is preserved unchanged.

Reserve 2 bits for expressing object layout

We would like to make instance variable reads in the JIT compiler faster
(as well as simplify the JIT implementation).  Currently, in order to
read an instance variable, we have to:

1. Test for heap object
2. Load object to a 64 bit register
3. Mask the object header
4. Bit test against the masked header
5. JNE
6. Load field

We would like to:

1. Test for heap object
2. Load object shape to a 32 bit register
3. Bit test against the shape
4. JNE
5. Load field

The way we fetch instance variables is not consistent across objects.
In order to realize our goal, we need to encode object layout inside the
shape.  If we encode object layout inside the shape, then the shape
itself will guarantee that the access pattern generated by the JIT
compiler is correct.

agentHost: batch AHP log writes and skip URI deep clone

Two perf fixes for AhpJsonlLogger, the per-message JSONL transport
logger. CPU traces of the agents window under heavy AHP traffic showed
~23% of wall time in MajorGC, dominated by VSBuffer allocations from
renderer-side writeFile IPCs and the recursive _replaceUris deep clone
applied to every message before JSON.stringify.

- log() now appends to a pending buffer list and schedules a single
  drain on the write queue. While a writeFile is in flight, all
  subsequent log() calls accumulate and land in the next drain via
  VSBuffer.concat, capped at 1 MiB per write. Rotation is still
  checked per entry, and flush()/ordering semantics are preserved
  via a _drainScheduled invariant.
- stringifyAhpLogEntry() now uses a JSON.stringify replacer instead
  of a tree-walking deep clone. URI.toJSON() stamps the output with
  $mid: MarshalledId.Uri, which the replacer detects (guarded by
  isUriComponents) and rewrites to the canonical UR

otel: normalize gen_ai.response.model to match request format

Anthropic responses echo the same logical model with a different separator
(e.g. request 'claude-opus-4.6' resolves to 'claude-opus-4-6'), causing
GROUP BY / DISTINCT on gen_ai.response.model to produce duplicate rows.

Add normalizeResponseModel(requestModel, responseModel) that echoes the
request value when the two strings only differ in '.' vs '-', and returns
the resolved value unchanged when it adds real specificity (e.g.
'gpt-5.4-mini' -> 'gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17'). Wire into the three call
sites that set gen_ai.response.model: chatMLFetcher (chat spans),
toolCallingLoop (foreground invoke_agent), and claudeOTelTracker
(Claude invoke_agent).

Fixes #318805

Make Linux desktop sanity tests robust to mid-test failures (#318850)

The Linux desktop sanity tests (deb/rpm/snap) ran cleanup unconditionally
after `testDesktopApp` without a try/finally, so when that step threw
(e.g. extension install flake tracked in microsoft/vscode-engineering#2877)
the uninstall step was skipped. Mocha then retried the test, the install
step hit `package code-insiders is already installed`, and the retry
masked the real failure with a misleading error
(microsoft/vscode-engineering#2878).

Fix:
- Wrap install/test/uninstall in try/finally so cleanup runs even when
  the test body throws.
- Make the uninstall helpers idempotent by detecting whether the package
  binary exists; this lets the finally block run safely even if install
  itself fails (and avoids double-uninstall on the happy path).
- Add a pre-install assertion to each install helper that fails fast
  with a clear diagnostic when the package is already present, so any
  leftover state from a prior kil

  prompts containing multimodal placeholder tokens without actual

all-missing result early. Affects both the masked and non-masked engines.

BUG: unstack corrupting source DataFrame via Copy-on-Write aliasing

The zero-copy fast path added in GH-65107 makes _Unstacker.get_new_values
return a view of the block values when the MultiIndex is already sorted.
For multi-block (non-consolidated) frames, Block._unstack built the result
block with refs=None, so Copy-on-Write did not track the sharing and
mutating the unstack result wrote through to the source DataFrame.

Track the reference when the unstacked values alias self.values, mirroring
the add_references logic in _Unstacker.get_result, so the zero-copy view is
preserved and CoW triggers a copy before either object is mutated.

The uniform-dtype fast path added in GH-64958 derived the column count

that width. A longer first row raised IndexError; a shorter first row
silently dropped trailing values. Gate the fast path on uniform row
lengths so ragged rows fall through to the object/pad path and are
padded to max width with NaN, matching list-of-lists behavior.

Fix WorktreeCreatedTaskDispatcher overfiring on restored sessions (#318241)

Introduce onDidStartSession event to distinguish sessions we just started from sessions that appear in the catalog (via cloud sync, refresh, etc).

Problem:
WorktreeCreatedTaskDispatcher listened to onDidChangeSessions and tried to filter on status=Untitled to identify newly started sessions. This was wrong because:
- Agent-host sessions are never Untitled when arriving via change events (skeleton gets setStatus(InProgress) before firing)
- onDidChangeSessions fires for any catalog change including cloud-synced/restored sessions from other devices
- This caused tasks to run for existing sessions on every sync, not just newly started ones

Solution:
- Add onDidStartSession: Event<ISession> to ISessionsManagementService
- Fire it from sendNewChatRequest after provider.sendRequest() resolves with committed session
- Rewrite WorktreeCreatedTaskDispatcher to listen ONLY to onDidStartSession instead of added/changed

PERF: build recode_for_groupby mapping with scatter + take_nd

Build the old->new code mapping by integer scatter-assignment and apply it with take_nd, avoiding the get_indexer_for hash lookup over the categories. This keeps the high-cardinality speedup while matching the prior behavior on low-cardinality and integer-keyed inputs. Add an O(1) short-circuit returning the input unchanged when every category is observed and already sorted.

Also add a whatsnew note and a regression test for grouping by an all-NaN Categorical, including the empty-categories case (GH#48749).

Update `shortcircuit_if_known` to `eval_shortcircuit()` (#94163)

Originally this PR was a comment fix that was flagged by @bgw's Claude:

```

  ▎ "Otherwise returns None."

  The function actually returns item_value(last_item) when no element matches.
  Comment doesn't describe behavior.

  ---
  The two most consequential bugs are #1 (swapped AND/OR predicates) and #2 
  (regex). #1 silently produces wrong nullishness/string-ness results for any
  code path that asks about &&/|| chains and feeds into linker decisions; #2
  silently corrupts every default-filter require.context resolution.
``` 

Related to #94159, updates the comment to say that it returns the last
item.

Which appears to be what is happening:

```rust
if it.peek().is_none() {
    return item_value(item);
} 
```

Afterwards, it now includes a reworking of `shortcircuit_if_known` into
`eval_shortcircuit()`:
https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/94163#discussion_r3313537931

Remove dead code from `JsValue::Binary` in `is_truthy` (#94165)

This is another thing flagged by @bgw's Claude:

```
  3. Dead duplicate match arm in is_truthy for StrictEqual (lines 2469–2494)

  ( … StrictEqual, Constant(a), Constant(b)) if a.is_value_type() => Some(a ==
  b),
  ( … StrictEqual, Constant(a), Constant(b)) if a.is_value_type() => { /* 
  same-type check */ }

  Identical pattern + guard. The second arm — the only one that handles
  cross-type equality conservatively — is unreachable. Looks like a half-applied
   fix.
``` 

I've removed the second arm with a double type check. Tests appear to
still pass and I can't think of a case where we'd hit the second arm.

REF: make TimedeltaArray.total_seconds match the scalar at all magnitudes

The vectorized path computed asi8 / pps, which rounds at the nanosecond
magnitude and so disagreed with Timedelta.total_seconds by 1 ulp for ns
values above 2**53 (only the integer-second boundary case matched).
Mirror the scalar's `int_seconds + sub_ns / 1e9` split via divmod so the
results are identical at every magnitude, and gate the nextafter boundary
nudge on |asi8| > 2**53, the only regime where the collapse can occur
(GH#46819).

Also drop a duplicate whatsnew entry that misattributed the fix to the
closed GH#31043 (dateutil DST), and note the index/Series.dt variants in
the notable-bug-fixes section.

Fix IVF dynamic visit ratio when rescore oversample is active (#148367)

* Pass originalK to IVF query for search strategy

Adds an originalK parameter to IVFKnnFloatVectorQuery to preserve the
pre-oversample k value. The search strategy now uses originalK instead
of the adjusted k, ensuring correct behavior when oversampling is applied.

* Replace originalK param with overSampleFactor

Passes the oversample factor instead of the pre-computed originalK to IVF
query constructors, letting each query derive originalK internally. This
simplifies the API and keeps the oversampling logic centralized.

* Fix IVF oversample factor for all query types

Resolves a merge conflict between oversample and slice routing support
by passing the overSampleFactor parameter to all IVF KNN query variants,
including sliced, diversifying, and standard queries.

Move SAML metadata resolution to background thread (#150037)

OpenSAML has very coarse grained locking - for example
`AbstractInitializableComponent.isInitialized` is `synchronized`

That can lead to threads being blocked if they attempt to interact
with the `AbstractReloadingMetadataResolver`, particularly if it is
resolving metadata at the time (which may involve network calls).

This commit changes the `SamlRealm` to _never_ interact directly with
the OpenSAML resolver. Instead, a periodic (60s) task calls the
resolver and sets the resolved entity descriptor into a cached value
that the SamlRealm can use.
